findings.trigger: Strict tenancy is on and the caller passes a persisted owner whose key attribute differs from getRawOriginal (getKey()/getMorphClass() changed after load). assertOwner reloads and checks only the raw owner when the resolver implements ResolvesOwnerTenant.
findings.consequence: Lookup and insert use the mutated owner identity. A current-tenant caller can bind the unique (owner_type, owner_id, profile) drive to another principal whose tenant was never checked. If that principal has no drive yet, provision persists the spoofed owner id under the caller's tenant; the real owner's later lookup hits that winner and assertDrive hides it, so no second drive is created. Passing the other owner model directly would have failed the fresh tenant check; the attribute swap bypasses it.
findings.evidence: TenancyBoundary::assertOwner (packages/core/src/Tenancy/TenancyBoundary.php:66) loads whereKey(getRawOriginal). DriveReadRepository::forOwner (line 62-65) then queries owner_id = getKey(). DriveProvisioner::provision (packages/drive/src/DriveProvisioner.php:93-94) inserts that same getKey()/getMorphClass(). DriveHandleFactory::owner (packages/drive/src/DriveHandleFactory.php:57) only rejects a null getKey(). Node/drive boundaries in this workset already ignore mutated keys; the owner path does not.
findings.direction: Resolve one fresh owner by the raw key, reject the call when the attribute key or morph class differs, and use only that fresh owner_type/owner_id for lookup, unique-race re-read, and insert.

findings.trigger: Strict tenancy is on and a child row shares drive_id and parent_id with an authorized node but its tenant_id stamp is null or not the owning drive's tenant.
findings.consequence: children(), search(), trashed(), and constrain() hide the mismatched child via the tenant predicate. descendants(), subtree(), ancestors(), and breadcrumb() reload only the root through scopedNode()/assertNode(), then walk the adjacency relation with no child stamp predicate, so trash/copy/subtree callers still observe and can mutate the mismatched row.
findings.evidence: descendants() line 137, subtree() line 161, ancestors() line 233, and breadcrumb() line 257 call the unscoped relation after scopedNode() (line 685-692), which checks only the root. StampsDriveTenant prevents new creates from writing a mismatched stamp; this is the existing-row denial gap.
findings.direction: After the root assert, run those walks through the same owning-drive plus child-stamp predicate used by constrain(), and fail the tree operation when a linked child stamp disagrees.
